title: Conductor Field Notebook: Run & Recovery
content:
Purpose:
A compact, practical running-notes doc for the engineer who executes a cross-functional canary / A/B exposure. This is intentionally informal: quick checks, hard thresholds, short recovery recipes, and message templates. Treat it as the thing you open on your laptop when youre on the hotseat.

Preflight (T-48h to T-30m):
- Confirm stakeholders: owner, PM, SRE oncall, observability lead, ops runbook owner. Post names + mobile pins in the experiment ticket.
- Capture baseline snapshot: pull last 72h median and p95 latency, error rate, 1h token spend. Save screenshots and paste into ticket.
- Cohort mapping: write down cohort ids, bucketing rule, and region mapping. Ensure cohort selector is deterministic for replay.
- Synthetic smoke: replay ~10k synthetic sessions (mix short/med/long seq) against control and canary. Expect p95 canary <= baseline p95 * 1.15. Flag otherwise.
- Quick quality check: run 12 representative prompts across intents; paste outputs into ticket for PM review.
- Rollback artifact check: confirm exact config ID to revert to, feature-flag key, infra commit hash, and database flags. Store commands in ticket.
- Communication plan: Slack channel, pager escalation order, and notification cadence (T+15, T+60, T+6h, T+24h).

Run timeline (concise):
- T-0: open channel, set transparent status message. Activate canary to 1-2% traffic.
- T+5m: verify basic health (all pods > 1/1, no new deployments in past 2m).
- T+15m: metrics check (errors, latency, business KPIs). If green -> increase to 5%.
- T+45m: if green -> increase to target slice or begin ramp schedule.
- T+1h: run lightweight manual evaluation sweep (20 focused prompts).
- T+6h: evaluate retention metrics & cost drift.
- T+24h: final decision checkpoint for full rollout or revert.

Gating thresholds (hard/fast heuristics):
- Error rate: revert immediately if rolling-window error rate > max(3x baseline, baseline + 0.8 percentage points). Example: baseline 0.2% -> rollback if >0.8% or >0.6% (3x) whichever is smaller/clear to ops.
- Latency (p95): pause if p95 increases > 30% relative or absolute increase > 200ms.
- Business signal: any measurable drop in top conversion metric > 5% in a 1h sliding window -> pause and investigate.
- Quality regressions: if manual eval samples show > 6/20 obvious regressions (hallucination, truncation, toxic output) escalate and rollback.
- Cost drift: token cost per request up > 20% sustained across 1h -> investigate pricing/quantization fallback.

Quick troubleshooting checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Check infra health: kubectl get pods -n rollout; describe failing pods.
2) Check autoscaler events and OOMs: kubectl get hpa, check node pressure.
3) Check model-serving logs: tail last 500 lines for the model shard.
4) Validate routing: confirm feature flag evaluated to correct cohort (curl feature-flag service).
5) Compare canary vs control traces for a failing request (trace id from APM).
6) If traffic spike, temporarily reduce canary weight to 0.1% while investigating.

Recovery recipes (fast commands & notes):
- Immediate stop & revert feature-flag (safest):
  curl -XPOST https://flags.redwood.ai/api/toggle -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"exp-123-canary","state":"off"}'
  (replace with internal toggle tool if required)
- Infrastructure rollback (if config issue):
  kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-serving -n inference --to-revision=REV
- Routing fallback to previous model variant: update traffic table via console or:
  curl -XPOST https://platform.redwood.ai/api/route -d '{"model":"gptx-1.0-stable","weight":1.0}'
- Circuit breaker: flip per-region limiter to "conservative" to reduce burst throughput.

Communication swatches (use these in Slack thread + email):
- Slack initial: "[RUN] Rolling canary exp-123 -> 1% at 2026-03-12T14:00Z. Owner: Rina A. Channel: #rollout-ops. Baseline p95=240ms, error=0.18%."
- Slack pause/rollback: "[PAUSE] Canaried exp-123 paused at 5% due to p95 ↑ 48% (baseline 240ms -> 356ms). Rolling back to control. Investigating. PagerXXX notified."
- Postmortem opener: short summary with timeline, leading hypothesis, mitigation, and next actions. Attach saved artifacts and queries.

Minimal queries (examples you can paste into the observability UI):
- Errors: alias(rate(error_count[5m]) / rate(request_count[5m]))
- Latency p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, svc))
- Token cost drift: sum(rate(cost_token_units[5m])) by (model) / sum(rate(request_count[5m]))
(Adjust vector names for current observability stack)

Manual quality check template (fill in during run):
- Prompt | Intent | Control output (notes) | Canary output (notes) | Verdict (ok/regress/blocker)
- Collect 20 rows; if >6 regressions -> escalate to PM + SRE.

Post-run:
- If rollout succeeded: capture final metric deltas vs baseline (p95, error, conversion, cost). Draft short TL;DR and add to ticket.
- If rolled back: collect traces, logs, and reproduce in staging. Schedule 24h blameless postmortem and action items.

Notes & heuristics from field:
- Synthetic runs are cheap and catch config-level regressions; they miss semantic regressions in tail intents. Always pair synth checks with small manual sweep.
- When in doubt about latency vs quality tradeoff, prefer quality for customer-facing flows, prefer latency for system-facing infra (e.g., support bots).
- Keep rollback steps atomic and idempotent; avoid multi-step half-rollbacks (they complicate state).
- If a regional issue looks like capacity, try regional fallback first instead of global rollback.

Open questions (placeholders to resolve after run):
- Should we auto-scale canary to 10% after 6h of green, or use manual approval?
- What is the absolute error rate trigger that should be standard across product teams?

Appendix: common decks & tickets to reference:
- experiment-framework-overview (confluence)
- JIRA-PLT-1423 (feature flag + rollout plan)
- rollout-scripts PR 278 (automation helpers)

End of notebook. Keep this doc as the ephemeral running notes for the active experiment and push a cleaned summary to Confluence after closure.
